rounds.proof_sketch: Mutation changes `input_width = input.size(3)` to `input_width = input.size(2)`. With fixed input shape [16, 32, 128, 128]: input.size(2) = 128 (height), input.size(3) = 128 (width). Since height == width == 128, both original and mutant assign input_width = 128. The mutation only produces different behavior when height ≠ width (non-square input), which is impossible under the fixed-shape contract.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutant survived because the fixed input shape [16, 32, 128, 128] is square (height = width = 128). The mutation substitutes `input.size(2)` for `input.size(3)`, but since both dimensions have identical values (128), the computed `input_width` is always correct. This affects all downstream computations: output_width calculation, bounds checking in the kernel (`w >= input_width`), and index calculation (`* input_width`). All these remain correct because the wrong dimension happens to equal the correct dimension. No value-level variation can expose this bug since it's purely a dimensional/shape issue.
rounds.kill_strategy: UNKILLABLE under fixed-shape contract. The mutation can only be killed by providing a non-square input tensor where height ≠ width (e.g., shape [16, 32, 128, 64]). With square inputs, input.size(2) == input.size(3) makes the mutation semantically equivalent.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for kernels with dimensional parameters should include non-square tensor shapes in the test configuration matrix. This mutation demonstrates a critical class of shape-dependent bugs that are invisible when only square inputs are tested. Consider adding explicit shape diversity requirements (e.g., at least one dimension pair must differ) to the testing contract.
